tasks.task: Sort a batch of emails and draft replies in the owner's voice

items.when: Before the first batch, to save a guide to the owner's senders, reply voice and triage rules
When a batch of emails must be sorted into reply, delegate, decline, wait or file, with drafts
When the inbox can be read directly, to sort messages, check senders and draft replies unsent
When one reply is delicate, to get a second draft checked against samples of the owner's style
When a draft answers a complaint, to check every promise in it and flag the tone
When the owner wants to fire back an angry reply, to weigh it and choose one practical step
Before the batch goes for approval, to have a fresh reviewer read each reply as its recipient

tasks.task: Run the daily inbox and calendar check

items.when: Once or twice each working day, in about 30 to 45 minutes
When one day needs meeting briefs, an action register and a plan from the calendar and open work
When the owner wants one short briefing of what needs them today
When follow-ups fall due today and each needs a draft ready to approve

tasks.task: Clear an email backlog and set triage rules that stick

items.when: When hundreds of emails have piled up and rules are needed so it does not happen again
When the inbox can be read directly, to pull out what needs the owner and deadlines in threads
When the rules are unwritten, to capture them by asking the owner a few questions
When email runs the owner's day, to cut the overload and keep fewer priorities

tasks.task: Turn a transcript or rough notes into minutes and follow-ups

items.when: When there is only a recording, to get a transcript with who spoke first
When you have a transcript or notes and need one-page minutes with one owner and date per action
When you want a shorter version of the minutes to compare
When a guest or host deserves one short, specific thank-you after the meeting
When the owner takes rough notes in calls and wants fuller notes with no bot present
Before the minutes go out, to check each decision and action against the transcript

tasks.task: Write the agenda for the next meeting

items.when: When a meeting is proposed, to decide whether to hold it, cost it and time the agenda
When one meeting must run from pre-read to notes with owners and dates
When attendees need an agenda and pre-read drawn from existing pages
When a status meeting may not be needed, to turn it into a short written update

tasks.task: Keep an action tracker across several meetings

items.when: When each meeting's actions must carry one owner and one date into the tracker
When actions sit across notes and email threads and must become one list with sources
Each week, to check last week's open actions and set the next agenda
When actions fall due, to draft the nudge for each owner

tasks.task: Write a one-page briefing note before an important meeting

items.when: When the owner has a meeting that matters and must walk in knowing the aim and the people
When there are notes on file and you need a sourced brief with open decisions and gaps
When little is known about the other side, to build a sourced file on the company or person
When rapport matters more than facts, to find what they care about and one good question
Before the note is handed over, to tie each fact about the other side to a dated source

tasks.task: Build a trip itinerary from booking confirmations

items.when: When flights, trains, hotels and meetings are booked and need one day-by-day plan with gaps spotted
When meetings on the trip cross time zones and slots must be offered to others
When free time on the trip needs a sourced plan with stops, breaks and alternatives

tasks.task: Plan the week from the calendar and the to-do list

items.when: Sunday evening or Monday morning, to turn a full calendar and long list into a week that fits
When you want a second plan built a different way to compare
When one day needs protected focus blocks and shallow work cut back
At the end of the week, to close open loops and find stalled projects
When weeks keep overrunning, to count what was chosen and what was taken, and win back an hour

tasks.task: Schedule meetings across calendars and time zones

items.when: When several people must meet, to sort time zones, check calendars and offer the best slots
When a new enquiry asks to meet, to answer it with a draft reply and real meeting times
Before the invite goes out, to check the meeting is worth holding at all

tasks.task: Write a polite chase, delay or decline

items.when: When someone owes a reply, a document or a payment, or the owner must push back or say no
When the no is hard, to give real reasons, a fairness check and another way forward
When earlier chasers were ignored, to try a version where a no still moves things on
When several invoices are unpaid, to get a reminder for each, gentle or firm to suit
Before sending, to have a fresh reviewer read it as the person being chased or declined

tasks.task: Write a formal complaint, refund or dispute letter

items.when: Before writing, to get the facts of the problem into one sheet with dates
When a company, landlord, agent or council must take a complaint or request seriously
When the first letter got no answer, to try a differently framed version to compare
When the owner is angry, to state the other side's view first and ask how the fix will work
Before sending, to tie every fact in the letter to a dated receipt, message or contract term
Before sending, to have a fresh reviewer read it as the complaints team receiving it

tasks.task: Take a complaint from first letter to resolution

items.when: When a first informal request has not fixed it and the complaint must be escalated in steps
When the record is scattered across emails, to get a dated timeline with key events marked
When the complaint has become a formal dispute and needs a fact sheet and a demand draft
When the other side replies with a formal letter, to read its claims and the reply options

tasks.task: Check a payment or bank-detail request before anyone acts

items.when: When a message asks to pay new bank details, pay urgently, wire money or buy gift cards
When the request comes with an invoice, to recalculate it and list missing fields and odd dates
When money or details were already sent, to set severity, who to tell and what to keep

tasks.task: Set up filing, naming and the yearly admin calendar

items.when: When a small office needs a folder tree, a naming rule and a yearly admin calendar
When an existing folder is a mess, to get a clean plan and duplicates found before anything moves
When the calendar must include company filings and their due dates
When everything is kept just in case, to sort by category and give what stays a home

tasks.task: Clean up a messy list or spreadsheet

items.when: When a list must be cleaned with every fix flagged and nothing deleted
When a sheet has stray spaces, text numbers, mixed dates and duplicates
When the same list arrives each month, to fix, re-check and save the rules
When the list is cleaned, to report gaps, duplicates and odd values left

tasks.task: Prepare expenses and chase unpaid invoices

items.when: When receipts and notes must become a report with totals by category and gaps to fix
When the bookkeeper needs a categorised file, receipt gaps and a reconciliation summary
Each week, to see who to chase, a reminder for each and a 90-day cash view
Before a supplier invoice is passed for payment, to recalculate each line and total

tasks.task: Track subscriptions, renewals and notice dates

items.when: When nobody knows what is being paid for, to get a register and savings options
When a software contract is up for renewal, to flag renewal traps and price rises
Each month, to see what changed, notice deadlines and proposed actions for the owner

tasks.task: Fill forms and handle PDFs and scans

items.when: When a PDF must be filled, merged, split or redacted with the original kept safe
When a letter or form is a scan and its text is needed
When a form lives on a website and must be filled and a copy saved

tasks.task: Summarise a long document or thread for the owner

items.when: When a long text or several must be cut to a short summary at a chosen level of detail
When the owner needs the answer first, the impact in numbers and the decision needed
When the document is a contract and the owner needs what each side owes

tasks.task: Write an office procedure or a handover note

items.when: When a routine lives in one head and needs a written procedure with who does what
When one repeat task needs exact steps, fixes if it fails and who to call
When work passes to someone else and they must be able to run from the note on day one
When someone goes on leave, to get a coverage map and task-by-task handover notes

tasks.task: Proofread a draft before the owner sends it

items.when: When a letter or document must be corrected in the owner's own voice with a log of changes
When there are samples of the owner's emails, to check a draft against their usual style

always.when: Before anything goes out in the owner's name, to catch typos and names spelt two ways

helpers.when: When receipts and invoices must be coded, reconciled and entered in the books
When the list needs formulas, lookups or a tracker built, not only a clean-up
When the owner needs a decision brief, board update or goals, not admin
When the job is an event with venue, suppliers and a run sheet
When a contract needs a full plain summary and a list of questions for a lawyer
When a repeat admin task should run by itself between the owner's tools

gaps: No library item learns one person's writing voice from their past emails and keeps it for later replies
No library item builds an itinerary from booking confirmations and spots tight connections or missing bookings
No library item writes a consumer complaint, refund or repair letter; the legal letter items are for formal disputes
No library item explains where to escalate a complaint: the ombudsman, regulator or scheme for each sector and country
No library item builds a yearly admin calendar for a small office: insurance, licences, tax dates and renewals
No library item answers an official form or application from the owner's own records
No library item checks a payment or bank-detail change request for fraud signs; only the kit prompt does
No library item designs a folder tree and file naming rule from scratch; the one that exists tidies a folder
No library item scripts a phone call to chase, complain or cancel
No library item gives clearly different versions of a hard letter, such as firm, conciliatory and final notice
No library item researches and shortlists options for errands such as gifts, restaurants or a local service
